title: Dynamic clicking sensitivity starting range
summary: For dynamic clicking, a practical starting range is about 30-45 cm/360 so you can balance anticipatory placement with quick path corrections.
why: Dynamic clicking sits between stable placement and moving-target correction, so it usually benefits from a middle-ground range instead of extreme speed or extreme stability.
The best setting is the one that lets you lead paths cleanly without chasing with large extra movement.
actions: Start around 37 cm/360 and slow down slightly if you keep chasing the path with large corrective movement.
If you are late to every path change even when your reads are correct, test a slightly faster step.
Watch where your crosshair is placed before the click, not just whether the shot landed.
avoid: Do not choose a setting that forces constant late chases on moving targets.
Avoid judging the setup only by single-shot speed if your placement gets worse.

drills.label: Dynamic placement check
drills.reason: Dynamic clicking shows quickly whether the chosen sens supports anticipatory placement or late chase behavior.

evidence.claim: Dynamic clicking emphasizes anticipatory placement and precision on moving targets, which supports using a balanced middle range.
evidence.excerpt: Putting your crosshair where the target will be instead of where it is is the single most important skill in this subcategory.
